---
title: "CLI Commands"
---

`carrier` exposes four subcommands. All of them exit non-zero and print `error: ...` to stderr on failure.

## `carrier init`

``` bash
carrier init <name> [--dir-name <dir>]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<name>` | Module name. Used as the default project directory (`<name>-proj`), the default source directory name, and the `name` field in `carrier.toml`. |
| `--dir-name <dir>` | Override the project directory name. |

Once the command is executed, it then creates `carrier.toml`, `README.md`, and `<name>/__init__.R`. Fails if the target directory already exists. 

## `carrier bundle`

``` bash
carrier bundle <path> [--rmbx]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<path>` | Project root (the directory containing `carrier.toml`). Usually `.`. |
| `--rmbx` | Produce a `.rmbx` archive instead of the default `.tar.gz`. |

::: {.callout-note title="Technical Notes"}
Do not bundle anything to `.rmbx`, yet. It is supposedly an analogue for `.whl` in Python and planned to be scrapped
:::

This command reads `carrier.toml`, then resolves the source directory (see [Module Structure](module-structure.qmd)), and writes `<name>_<version>.<ext>` to the current working directory. It fails if the source directory has no files, or if `carrier.toml` is missing or malformed.

## `carrier install`

``` bash
carrier install <source> [--install-deps]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<source>` | One of: a directory containing `carrier.toml`, a `.tar.gz` archive, or `gh:user/repo` (optionally `gh:user/repo/tree/branch/subpath`). |
| `--install-deps` | Actually install resolved R package dependencies from CRAN, rather than only printing the plan. |

Any existing install of the same module name is replaced. The `[package_deps]` / `[module_deps]` in `carrier.toml` are resolved and printed regardless of `--install-deps`; without the flag, R packages are planned but not fetched.

`gh:` sources require the `network` feature on `carrier-core`. See [Installation](../installation.qmd). The GitHub tarball fetch is unauthenticated, so repeated `gh:` installs in a short window (e.g. CI) can hit GitHub's rate limit. Right now, it shows up as a plain HTTP-status error, rather than a rate-limit-specific message.

## `carrier remove`

``` bash
carrier remove <name> [--force]
```

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<name>` | Name of an installed module. |
| `--force` | Skip the `[y/N]` confirmation prompt. |

Fails if no module with that name is installed.
